wintercity_e12_entry.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_entry.text: On Day 892, Yue reached Bai Jia's stall after the paid technician had cleared the repaired flue. The shutter was open and the old queue had a new bend around the inspected stove. Jia had moved a table so customers would not lean against the hot pipe. Yue stood on the public side and ordered the ordinary bowl. Being present at a reopening did not give her the technician's authority or a reason to test the heat with her injured hand.

wintercity_e12_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_001.text: Jia noticed the support and set the bowl within easy reach. She asked whether a spoon with a thicker handle would help. Yue accepted it, paying the same two-copper meal price printed for everyone. The handle belonged to the stall and stayed there afterward. Jia told her about losing a morning's trade during inspection and having the repair cost entered before reopening. The account sounded less triumphant than a tale of heroic intervention. Its actual customers could now sit under a working flue.

wintercity_e12_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_002.text: A regular customer complained that the larger table took his favourite place. Jia offered the remaining seats and declined to move the inspected clearance. Yue did not speak for the stall. The customer chose to eat standing by the window and stayed long enough to describe the weather beyond the north gate. People could be annoyed by a safe ordinary arrangement without becoming villains whose inconvenience Yue had to defeat. She listened while the bowl cooled.

wintercity_e12_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_003.text: Outside, the older ice had narrowed to strips along the wall. Yue used the clinic's light route, avoiding the steep cut across the yard. A handcart team passed carrying fuel under a covered tally. The driver stopped at the crossing rather than asking the waiting pedestrians to scatter. Yue could recognise the source yard's inventory mark but had no current claim on the cart. Her own earlier instrument issue had been returned and closed, with neither its residual fuel nor its deposit left to spend.

wintercity_e12_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_004.text: At the heat court, Qiao Ning answered the waiting-space question Yue had left before Day 891 ended. An injured worker could use the public open waiting bench under the same actual opening hours; no employment badge was required there. The inspected paid rooms still had their own finite bookings and limits. The answer did not create another room or erase an owner's private calendar. Yue copied the useful public hours slowly with her uninjured hand and stopped before stiffness made the line crooked.

wintercity_e12_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_005.text: An ordinary queue dispute began near the clerk's window. Two people both believed they had been sent first from the outer gate. Ning asked for the actual numbered slips. One had yesterday's date and needed a new place; the other held today's earlier number. Yue could see the dispute settle without lending it her losing score. The clerk's authority came from the appointment list. A public desk did not need every question to be a judgment of the owner she had faced.

wintercity_e12_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_006.text: On Day 893, Yue paid the usual separate food charge before going back upstairs. Mrs Fen had left a clean ordinary cover for the support at the door; the clinic instructions allowed changing the outside cloth without removing its fitted support. Yue asked for help with the fastening and thanked her afterward. She could make a bounded request without surrendering the rest of her day. She also could not turn the innkeeper's unbilled kindness into an unlimited promise of future care.

wintercity_e12_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_007.text: The morning took more patience than the walking distance suggested. Yue read two pages, then put the book down when her posture began to load the forearm. The clinic restriction concerned the actual strain, not merely her willingness to work. Holding a light object all morning could still become an avoidable load. She found that harder to accept than the clear prohibition on powered practice. The small circuit remained hers, while this route stayed unused pending review.

wintercity_e12_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_008.text: The neighbour at the next room wanted to borrow her support to show someone how it was tied. Yue declined because she needed the actual fitted support and a demonstration could use another strip of cloth. The neighbour found one at the wash bench. No friendship was broken by the answer. Yue watched the ordinary explanation from the doorway, then returned to her chair when the audience wanted to make the story longer than her arm could comfortably tolerate.

wintercity_e12_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_009.text: The afternoon's public notice advertised temporary oral reading for the cold-term desk. A fixed fund would pay two copper per hour for staff to read already public notices to callers who could not comfortably read them. The keeper would do the writing and manage the queue. Yue was not being hired to certify apparatus, gather testimony, or promise access to private rooms. Three limited mornings might fit the clinician's ordinary light-work restriction, if the desk could maintain its stated load limit.

wintercity_e12_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_010.text: She did not accept from the notice alone. Qiao Ning showed the task place: a seated reader with a document stand, no carried registers, no heavy shutters to lift, and a keeper available for written entries. There would be two hours on each of Days 895, 896, and 897, with a rest after the first half-hour and later breaks. The six completed hours would earn twelve copper. A missed hour would remain unpaid unless a separately agreed reason changed the account.

wintercity_e12_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_011.text: Ning said the short appointment was not the same as the later seasonal commission now being planned. That longer work would need its own authorization and staffing. Yue could earn twelve from this small completed interval without acquiring a permanent public job. The desk offered her one of the available seats and would allocate it to the next eligible reader if she declined before the roster closed. The grant was finite; it would not pay three different people for the same one-person slot.

wintercity_e12_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_012.text: Yue went back to the clinic desk to check the physical fit of the task. The attendant read the existing restriction and said an ordinary seated reading interval could be attempted within the written limits, stopping if the strain increased. That was not a new powered clearance or a guarantee of painless work. The task keeper would need to honour the breaks and use another person for carrying. Yue asked for that condition to be put on the appointment, rather than rely on a sympathetic conversation.

wintercity_e12_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_013.text: Du Ling had a different short request. The washhouse wanted a volunteer to speak the verified public service hours to customers waiting outside, for the same three mornings. Its keeper would do all lifting and keep the paid attendants on their own work. The role carried no wages and needed five copper in actual meals and return crossings over the three days. Ling offered the work without making it a condition of anyone's washhouse entry. Yue could decline and the regular notice board would still stand.

wintercity_e12_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_014.text: Ling did not call the volunteer an official delegate. The customers would receive the same verified timetable Yue could read publicly, with questions beyond it sent to the proper desk. The role would give Yue ordinary contact with people the public copying office rarely saw. It could not create testimony consent or turn washhouse customers into her later witnesses. She went to see the sheltered waiting place and checked that it had a seat and no expectation of moving the coal bucket.

wintercity_e12_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_015.text: A quieter alternative remained available at the inn. Yue could decline both finite morning roles, buy three copper in simple additional meals, and keep the interval light until the Day 898 review. Mrs Fen could provide the ordinary food at that listed price, but not promise a healer's service. No work wage would be earned. Yue would keep the unpaid hours and avoid a public appointment whose actual demands she was not yet sure she could tolerate.

wintercity_e12_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_016.text: On Day 894, she read the three offers in the public window, then set them beside the current clinic note. Each preserved the affected arm's restriction; each used the same mornings differently. Reading would earn a finite wage and require a public seat at its booked times. Volunteering would spend five copper and create a bounded promise to the washhouse queue. Quiet recovery would cost three in extra food and leave the mornings unbooked. None changed her physical defeat or earned a new spiritual stage.

wintercity_e12_017.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_017.text: Rui Wen stopped by before the offers had to be answered. She did not select one for her. She asked what she most wanted from the coming mornings and whether the actual load limits had been checked. Yue said money mattered, company mattered, and the bruise made both questions feel like an argument with her own patience. Wen said those were different needs, then left for her repairs. She could choose a real tradeoff without finding a sentence that made every option equally profitable.

wintercity_recovery_choice.speaker: narrator
wintercity_recovery_choice.text: The public roster would close that evening. Yue could accept the paid seated reading within its stated restriction, promise the washhouse's limited volunteer mornings, or keep the mornings for ordinary rest. The unchosen paid seat would go to another eligible reader. Ling would keep the notice board when no volunteer came. The inn would not charge the extra food unless ordered. She signed one answer for the actual Days 895 through 897, leaving the other people's work to them.

choices.text: Take the six-hour seated public-reading appointment for twelve copper, with enforced breaks.
Give three seated mornings to the washhouse queue and spend five copper on meals and crossings.
Keep the mornings for restricted recovery and buy three copper in extra simple meals.

wintercity_recovery_reading.speaker: narrator
wintercity_recovery_reading.text: Yue accepted the six-hour seated reading appointment and had the written breaks attached to its public roster. Ning assigned the unchosen applicants to their next available places rather than invent another copy of the same funded seat. On Day 895, Yue arrived with no carried register. The keeper set the public sheets on the stand. She began by reading the actual waiting hours, then answered a caller's request to repeat the location of the open bench.

wintercity_e12_reading_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_reading_001.text: After the first half-hour, she stopped for the booked rest. The keeper announced the interval and handled urgent numbered slips. Yue did not fill the pause with hurried writing because the task sounded too simple to justify care. A caller waited rather than have the facts guessed by another customer. The morning ended after two actual completed hours, with the time entered by the keeper. Her arm was tired in posture but no sharper in pain.

wintercity_e12_reading_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_reading_002.text: On Day 896, one caller asked for advice about an unpaid private heating bill. Yue could read the public dispute desk address but could not decide the bill from the notice. She directed the question to the appointed clerk. The caller disliked the answer and still accepted the address. Yue kept reading within the actual task, rather than buy the person's gratitude by promising a result no public reader had authority to deliver.

wintercity_e12_reading_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_reading_003.text: The last morning, Day 897, included a sheet that had been replaced overnight. Yue checked its date before reading and handed the superseded copy back to the keeper. The change concerned an earlier gate closing during maintenance. A stale sheet would have sent callers to a locked entrance. She completed the two hours with the appointed breaks, allowing the keeper to lift and file everything. This was ordinary useful work her restricted arm could currently tolerate.

wintercity_e12_reading_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_reading_004.text: The keeper paid twelve copper for the six actual hours, two per hour, and marked the short appointment complete. Yue took the wage receipt and her own nonconfidential observation about the replaced sheet. She held no customer file or official badge after closure. The pay belonged to completed reading, not to surviving a duel or endorsing an owner. Her five-copper volunteer expense and three-copper extra rest meals had not been bought on this selected path.

wintercity_e12_reading_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_reading_005.text: Before leaving, Yue asked whether the public stand could keep the current date visible for the next reader. Ning accepted the practical suggestion for the desk's own review, without promising a new funded job. Yue returned to the inn with a finite paid task closed and the same clinic review due tomorrow. The arm still needed its actual examination. Six quiet hours of useful work had not cleared it for spiritual force.

wintercity_recovery_volunteer.speaker: narrator
wintercity_recovery_volunteer.text: Yue promised the washhouse's three seated mornings and paid the actual five-copper meals and crossings in advance. She declined the public reader's funded seat; Ning gave it to the next eligible applicant. On Day 895, Ling placed a chair inside the sheltered waiting edge and assigned the ordinary attendant to carrying. Yue read the verified timetable to the first customers, explaining that she could speak only for the printed public hours.

wintercity_e12_volunteer_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_volunteer_001.text: A customer wanted to know whether attending would oblige her to support Yue at a hearing. Yue said no; there was no testimony request in this service task. Ling confirmed it before returning to the washhouse work. The customer used the information and made no promise about future disputes. Yue found the conversation easier afterward. A useful public answer could remain useful when the person receiving it kept every later choice of loyalty.

wintercity_e12_volunteer_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_volunteer_002.text: On Day 896, sleet drove the queue toward the inner shelter. Ling's paid keeper moved the chair and notice board; Yue did not carry either with the injured arm. The timetable remained the same, but its location changed within the approved shelter. Yue repeated where the waiting bench stood and sent a private billing question to the proper desk. She spent the scheduled interval speaking and sitting, not certifying the stove or gathering named customer stories.

wintercity_e12_volunteer_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_volunteer_003.text: The third morning, Day 897, an older caller misheard the afternoon opening as the early one. Yue repeated both times and asked which route the caller planned to use. The person chose the later opening after hearing the correct transfer interval. That small decision belonged to the caller. Yue could observe its practical effect without entering the person into a confidential file. The paid attendants kept their own tasks, with no wage silently transferred to a volunteer.

wintercity_e12_volunteer_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_volunteer_004.text: At closure, Ling checked the three actual mornings and thanked Yue without creating a payable employment account. The five copper had funded the selected meals and crossings and was spent. There was no twelve-copper reader wage, no new washhouse pass, and no permanent delegate mandate. Yue returned the timetable copy borrowed for the chair and kept only her own nonconfidential recollection. The ordinary notice board remained for future customers when she would not be there.

wintercity_e12_volunteer_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_volunteer_005.text: She returned to the inn with the same injured arm and Day 898 clinic appointment. The volunteering had bought no care priority or extra spiritual permission. It had given customers usable hours and made a finite promise real. Ling could choose whether to fund another helper later, and Yue could choose whether to accept another offer. Neither woman left the completed three mornings as a vague debt against every future day.

wintercity_recovery_rest.speaker: narrator
wintercity_recovery_rest.text: Yue declined both public morning roles before the roster closed. Ning allocated the funded reading seat to the next eligible person, and Ling kept the normal notice board at the washhouse. Yue bought the listed three copper in additional simple meals for Days 895 through 897. The food purchase did not include a clinician, a miracle medicine, or a guarantee of quicker recovery. It gave her an ordinary way to eat without adding another scheduled street task.

wintercity_e12_rest_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_rest_001.text: On Day 895, she sat by the inn window and watched the frost soften along the opposite rail. She did not use the empty hours for a secret powered rehearsal. The current restriction remained written beside her key. Reading a light page and changing position took place within the ordinary limits; she stopped when posture began to pull at the bruise. Having chosen rest did not require her to pretend that the arm felt well.

wintercity_e12_rest_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_rest_002.text: The public reader's voice reached the courtyard on Day 896. Someone else had taken the paid seat and was giving callers the verified hours. Yue felt a brief regret about the twelve copper she had chosen not to earn. She did not answer by asking the keeper to pay her for a parallel imagined task. Her quiet morning and paid extra food were the actual selected cost and benefit. The ordinary work outside remained genuinely done by another person.

wintercity_e12_rest_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_rest_003.text: Mrs Fen asked whether Yue wanted the lunchtime bowl brought upstairs. Yue accepted for the purchased meal and offered to leave the cleaned bowl at the door for collection. She did not assume all future food would be carried free. The innkeeper agreed to that bounded arrangement for the bought meals. A small ordinary convenience could help today without turning the inn into a perpetual recovery service or cancelling the next clinic fee.

wintercity_e12_rest_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_rest_004.text: On Day 897, Yue took the short clinic-approved walk after breakfast, carrying only the appointment slip. She could have passed the washhouse's sheltered queue but had no volunteer promise there. Ling's ordinary board was visible and the paid attendants were at work. Yue nodded from the street and returned to the inn. Declining the role had not deprived customers of every source of public information; it had left one finite possible addition unprovided.

wintercity_e12_rest_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_rest_005.text: The three extra meals were received and paid, with no unspent portion of that food order waiting to finance something else. Yue held no reader wage or washhouse mandate. The quiet interval had allowed less scheduled effort, and tomorrow's examination would establish what the arm could actually do. She gathered the Day 898 note with her reserved eight copper. Rest was a real choice of use and opportunity, not an invisible claim that nothing had happened.

wintercity_recovery_review_entry.speaker: narrator
wintercity_recovery_review_entry.text: On Day 898, Yue arrived at Zhou An's clinic with the eight copper already reserved for this review. The clinician checked what she had actually done over the three mornings rather than treating every kind of ordinary work as the same load. She described the selected activity and its real breaks. He inspected the bruising, asked about sensation, and tested limited movement. The injury had begun to settle; it had not vanished because an interval was completed.

wintercity_e12_after_001.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_001.text: The paid review cost eight copper and produced a narrower current permission. Light ordinary tasks could continue within the demonstrated range, with breaks and no lifting beyond the written limit. A controlled unloaded personal comparison would need a separate supervised review before the affected arm powered any apparatus. He booked that check for Day 912 at another eight-copper fee. Yue entered the actual future cost in her own account. Her established stage stayed seven, without being a substitute for the examination.

wintercity_e12_after_002.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_002.text: She asked whether she could carry a filled kettle. Zhou An said no under this current load note, even if she could carry an empty one briefly. The difference was weight and duration, not pride. He showed the safe position for ordinary fastening with the support and asked her to repeat it without force. A question small enough to answer accurately was more useful than asking when she would be able to do anything she wanted.

wintercity_e12_after_003.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_003.text: The clinician said there was no reliable promise that the bruise would be painless by a named festival. If symptoms worsened, she would seek another ordinary assessment rather than wait for the scheduled date. Yue accepted the uncertain instruction. A known date could reserve a place and money; it could not order tissue to recover. She left with paid care actually received and a limited next step, not a new spiritual exercise hidden inside a reassuring farewell.

wintercity_e12_after_004.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_004.text: At the inn, she showed Mrs Fen the present lifting restriction because the innkeeper sometimes asked residents to help move the water bucket. Fen crossed Yue off that ordinary rota until a later review allowed it. Another resident would receive the actual paid carrying interval instead. Yue did not ask to keep its wage after surrendering the work. The change made her own room easier to manage and left the bucket moved by someone who could safely lift it.

wintercity_e12_after_005.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_005.text: Wen came with a repaired umbrella whose handle could be held lightly, but did not ask Yue to carry it across town. She had a customer's messenger booked. They talked while it waited by the door, discussing the dark blue cloth that looked almost black indoors. Yue preferred it in sunlight. Wen said the buyer wanted exactly that uncertainty. Neither of them needed the conversation to prove a new political alliance. It was an ordinary object made for another person's chosen taste.

wintercity_e12_after_006.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_006.text: The weather turned to fine snow after the review. Yue watched people enter the sheltered lane with their own purposes, not all arranged around the contest's meaning. A young singer carried a covered instrument; the carrier's shoulder strap had been fitted for its weight. The student would audition after the cold festival and had not asked Yue for a reference. Yue could be interested without becoming the sponsor of every hopeful person who crossed the court.

wintercity_e12_after_007.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_007.text: When the inn's evening bell rang, she bought her ordinary meal and sat where the bench supported her back. A neighbour asked if the clinic had cleared everything. She gave the actual limited answer. The neighbour nodded and offered to shift a plate, then returned to arguing about next week's market price. Care did not have to make every conversation solemn. Yue was relieved to remain a person who could dislike overcooked greens as well as one with a supervised defeat behind her.

wintercity_e12_after_008.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_008.text: The public desk's seasonal proposal arrived as a draft rather than a wage guarantee. It planned three three-hour mornings each week for nine weeks, beginning Day 900 and ending Day 962. At two copper per hour, each completed week would pay eighteen; the maximum for all completed hours would be one hundred sixty-two. The grant had been authorized for oral public work, with separate paid keepers for writing and carrying. No wage was due merely because a draft had reached her room.

wintercity_e12_after_009.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_009.text: The work would explain existing public service notices, check that callers understood the route they intended to take, and send disputes to the proper clerk. It would not certify private apparatus or gather confidential worker testimony. The fund was independent of North Kestrel Works, so declining a factory proposal did not remove the authorized reader seat. Ning would select from eligible applicants after checking current restrictions. Yue had to apply and accept the actual terms; friendship with the clerk could not silently hire her.

wintercity_e12_after_010.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_010.text: The draft's hours began on Day 900, with the first week paid after the scheduled sessions on Days 900, 902, and 904. The pay desk would settle that completed week on Day 906. Similar seven-day intervals would follow if work was actually done, with the last sessions on Days 956, 958, and 960 paid on Day 962. Missed hours would remain unpaid unless an actual agreed rule applied. A fixed maximum was not a purse she could spend before earning it.

wintercity_e12_after_011.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_011.text: Yue checked that the first sessions could keep the arm unloaded and allow the current written breaks. Ning confirmed the role's seated stand, separate keeper, and ban on carrying registers. The clinic note would be part of the accepted staffing plan, without exposing private diagnosis details on the public notice. Yue asked for the public roster to show ordinary breaks as part of the schedule. Callers could plan around real pauses rather than depend on a tired reader forgetting to take them.

wintercity_e12_after_012.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_012.text: A second eligible reader wanted the same appointment. Yue spoke with her outside the desk and learned she preferred a later afternoon role because of mornings at home. Ning could not pay two people the full amount from this one funded slot. The afternoon proposal had its own unapproved budget and remained uncertain. Yue did not invent it as compensation to make applying feel harmless. The other reader chose whether to keep seeking work, with her own reasons that did not require Yue's consent.

wintercity_e12_after_013.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_013.text: The application asked for ordinary reading experience, current availability, and relevant task restrictions. Yue listed the public notices she had actually handled, rather than every heroic thing an audience might have claimed about the contest. The full private factory method was not part of her application. She had no permission to sell it as a public qualification. The form's questions did not require a declaration that she could overcome a Foundation practitioner; accurate oral work would be assessed on its actual demands.

wintercity_e12_after_014.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_014.text: Ning arranged a short public sample for the next morning, Day 899. No paid seasonal term would start before the applicant and desk actually accepted it. Yue put that appointment beside the Day 912 clinic check, reserving the eight-copper future fee separately from her journey money. The new possibility gave the coming weeks shape without curing the arm. She could seek suitable useful work and still follow a restriction that enthusiasm could not override.

wintercity_e12_after_015.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_015.text: Before bed, Yue wrote a short entry about the direct comparison. Gao Shen had won through a larger qualified physical capacity within the declared conditions. She had received competent prepared ordinary care after an actual strain. She could remember fear, shame, and the practical benefit of preparation without changing those facts. The owner might still be wrong about a service clause. Keeping that question open did not require pretending the bar had ever moved in her favour.

wintercity_e12_after_016.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_016.text: She folded the event score into the light cover. Its standard public information could be shown where relevant, while another person's private source stayed protected under its own permission. Her paid copy did not make every record in the city public. Yue had learned that restriction before this injury, and could still find it frustrating now. A clear boundary was not proof that the owner had won an argument he had never actually made.

wintercity_e12_after_017.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_017.text: On the notice board, the cold festival committee asked for ordinary songs and repaired puppets. Peng had already booked the paid frame helper. Yue could submit a spoken line for consideration if she wished, but had no reason to move the frame with her strained arm. She read a child's comic verse about a stove too proud to accept kindling. The line made her laugh. Peng said it might stay if the child consented and the rehearsal fit the running time.

wintercity_e12_after_018.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_018.text: The committee's ordinary choices were not determined by Yue's disagreement with North Kestrel Works. One member liked the stove joke, another worried it was too long, and the child wanted to keep the rhyme at the end. Yue listened while they found a shorter version with the same ending. No institutional reform occurred in the courtyard that evening. Something more modest did: several people managed to alter a line while allowing its young author a real answer.

wintercity_e12_after_019.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_019.text: Du Ling came to collect a public-hours sheet from the board. She said the washhouse had paid for repairs to a seat whose split edge caught clothing. Yue asked whether the affected customers had wanted the old seat kept. Ling said they had chosen repair rather than another small stool, and the carpenter had quoted a finite price. The ordinary decision changed where people could wait tomorrow. Yue could hear it without converting those customers into supporters for any future hearing.

wintercity_e12_after_020.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_020.text: At the outer gate, a carrier argued that the public entrance should remain open after the posted closing hour because his goods were useful. The keeper offered the actual after-hours delivery route and its separate charge. The carrier could accept, wait until morning, or take the goods elsewhere. Yue did not give him a fourth invented permission. Posted hours mattered partly because someone would otherwise have to remain on an unpaid shift so his urgency could stay convenient.

wintercity_e12_after_021.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_021.text: Her own private letter remained with the regular dispatch under the one-copper fee already paid. It would travel at the carrier's ordinary pace. She did not assume a reply had reached her mother or demand a second answer before the first arrived. The selected earlier family support had its actual finite amount and purpose, with a report still to come. Baseline help at home had not been conditional on Yue winning the contest or earning a new city wage.

wintercity_e12_after_022.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_022.text: Yue pictured her mother at the small kiln table, then checked the impulse to supply an imagined good day as if it were a received fact. The last known account said the shoulder still required shorter tasks and ordinary help. A later letter could change her knowledge. Until then, she could keep the current care commitment and refrain from spending the same gift again in another mental calculation. Concern was real even when certainty was unavailable.

wintercity_e12_after_023.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_023.text: The court's evening stove used ordinary authorized fuel from its keeper's stock. Yue could feel warmth without providing a spiritual charge herself. Hu Yan passed carrying a closed equipment list and asked about the next clinic date. She gave Day 912. He said any later apparatus booking would require the actual assessment and a new source account. The former test's accepted residual had returned to the yard; there was nothing lying unclaimed for a free renewed attempt.

wintercity_e12_after_024.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_024.text: He also said the apparatus would undergo a routine inspection before any next participant interval. Yue did not need to imagine it waiting eternally ready for her recovery. Public equipment had a service life, paid maintenance, and other applicants. When she asked whether a later observer place might be available, he directed her to the ordinary booking desk. Interest was permitted. Priority had not been awarded as compensation for defeat.

wintercity_e12_after_025.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_025.text: A neighbour described Gao Shen as unbeatable. Yue said the direct result had shown him stronger than her at that inspected task. She did not know every possible opponent or future condition. The neighbour wanted a broader story because it made the city easier to sort into winners and losers. Yue left the smaller true statement in place. Respecting the actual difference in capacity did not require declaring a universal rule she had no evidence to measure.

wintercity_e12_after_026.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_026.text: The innkeeper's assistant brought a repaired chair into the common room. Its missing rung had made the old seat unsafe, and the carpenter's bill showed the actual repair. Yue chose that chair only after Fen said it had been checked for ordinary use. She did not test it by throwing qi into its frame. Sitting comfortably was enough. The next reader appointment would ask her to attend to someone else's question, and she wanted one calm evening beforehand.

wintercity_e12_after_027.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_027.text: She counted the week's paid room interval and the separate meals already received. The lower eight-copper rate required seven days' notice and did not cover food or clinical care. Her existing booking ran through Day 891, so the next eight-copper week, Days 892 through 898, had been paid on its first morning. She checked the receipt against the date now. An injured person still needed a bed funded from real money; ordinary sympathy was not an entry in the inn's rent account.

wintercity_e12_after_028.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_028.text: The upcoming room week, Days 899 through 905, would likewise cost eight under the continuing notice arrangement. Yue reserved it from completed earnings, alongside the Day 912 fee and the separate thirty-two-copper travel sum. She could finance current costs without treating the seasonal draft as cash in hand. A later actual wage would replenish only what it actually paid. The numbers gave her less dramatic comfort than hope, but they would still be there when the candle went out.

wintercity_e12_after_029.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_029.text: At the market crossing, an apprentice had dropped a basket of small wooden toggles. Yue stayed out of the moving cart lane while the keeper stopped the traffic and the apprentice gathered them. She did not lean down repeatedly with the affected arm merely because the objects were light one by one. Another passerby helped without asking for a reward. The basket reached the bench with fewer scattered pieces, and the cart resumed when the crossing was clear.

wintercity_e12_after_030.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_030.text: One toggle had rolled under a shutter. The shopkeeper unlocked it after checking whose goods were being recovered, rather than break the wood for a hurried stranger. Yue admired how much ordinary cooperation depended on small explanations given in time. No one needed a higher realm for this task. No one needed to supply a lie that she had done the collecting. She continued her light walk while the apprentice counted the actual pieces back into the basket.

wintercity_e12_after_031.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_031.text: In the square, two musicians tried a festival tune at different speeds. A third asked which version dancers could follow on wet stone. They slowed it until the steps fit the smaller safe space. Yue listened from a bench, keeping the arm supported and leaving the musicians their own argument about style. The compromise was audible in the next attempt. A changed rhythm could matter greatly to the dancers who would actually have to keep pace.

wintercity_e12_after_032.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_032.text: An elderly listener disliked the slower version and said so. The musicians let him finish, then kept the speed their planned space required. Yue found it useful to see a complaint heard without becoming an order. She had sometimes confused another person's disappointment with a debt she must pay immediately. Here the music continued, and the listener stayed on the bench. Their disagreement did not require either side to disappear from the square.

wintercity_e12_after_033.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_033.text: Back at the inn, Fen measured the doorway curtain before buying new cloth. She asked Yue about the colour only, not to hold the heavy roll. Yue chose the warmer brown from two small samples. Fen had the actual price and would decide whether to purchase. The opinion gave Yue a place in ordinary room life without letting her spend the innkeeper's money or obliging her injured arm to do the installation.

wintercity_e12_after_034.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_034.text: The small sample looked different beside the existing wall. Yue said so when Fen returned, rather than defend her first preference as if changing it proved weakness. They checked it in daylight and chose the other cloth. Fen took the samples back to the seller under their actual return arrangement. The room would receive a different curtain because an ordinary comparison had changed a real purchase. Yue kept her first opinion without requiring the whole inn to live with it.

wintercity_e12_after_035.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_035.text: Before the lamp was trimmed, she set a fresh page beside the public sample notice. Tomorrow's keeper would do the written entries. Her own page was for short ordinary reminders within the restricted range, with no obligation to fill it. She left the unused space empty tonight.

wintercity_e12_after_036.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_036.text: The sample notice for tomorrow concerned a changed public gate route. Yue read it once aloud, took the planned pause, and checked the place names without carrying the stand. Her voice could remain steady while the arm rested. The task had no need for a concealed counter-movement exercise or a new spiritual source. She put the sheet back in its envelope, leaving the morning's actual assessment to occur at the appointed desk.

wintercity_e12_after_037.speaker: narrator
wintercity_e12_after_037.text: Sleep came before the room was completely quiet. Someone downstairs practised the festival drum pattern too quickly, then slowed at a neighbour's request. Yue turned without loading the support and waited for the ordinary ache to settle. Her coming work was possible because its real demands had been checked, not because injury had vanished from the account. The next day would start with that arm, the booked room, and an application she still had to earn.
